_about: PROPOSED default note layouts for 1 to 4 phones, for owner review. A song can say "layout": "default" to use these, or give its own layout. Keys starting with _ are comments. Each phone (A-D) holds exactly four notes, one per gesture; forward and back carry each phone's most-used notes.

1._why: Do Re Mi Sol covers the opening of most simple tunes. Fa, La and Ti are missing, so most songs need their own 1-phone layout.

2._why: Split by chord role, as the spec suggests: A holds the anchors (Do, Re, Sol, high Sol), B the colors (Mi, Fa, La, high Do). Every major chord gets at least two of its notes on different phones. Trade-offs: Ti is not on either phone; Do-Re and Mi-Fa are neighbors on the same phone, so some stepwise runs stay with one player.

3._why: Do up to high Sol (12 notes). Root, third and fifth of the I, IV and V chords (Do-Mi-Sol, Fa-La-Do, Sol-Ti-Re) always fall on three different phones, and each note keeps its octave on the same phone. Trade-offs: Do-Re, Mi-Fa and Sol-La are neighbors on the same phone; La2, Ti2 and Do3 are not available.

4._why: All 15 notes, plus Sol doubled on A and D as a safety net. I, IV, V, ii and vi chords all fall on different phones, and octave families stay together (A = the Do bell, B = Re/Mi, C = Fa/Ti, D = Sol/La). Trade-offs: Re-Mi and Sol-La are neighbors on the same phone, so a stepwise melody passes between players less often than with a strict interleave.
